format_note: Both forms need one field each that format v3 cannot express, proposed for the format revision that slice F adopts. 'capture': 'none' means TS delivers the source without an IPC capture and offers the form's invocation to its registration directly (no live native capture); Rust and Python read the invocation argument as for 'invocation': 'fixture'. 'current_model_edits' are edits (op 'set') applied to TS's current model only, which otherwise is the captured invocation's model; Rust and Python have no current-model input beyond 'requested'. Before the flip every language reads needs_recompute on both forms, so the entry is a difference only once the flags are set.

entry.description: A valid successor statement with its actual invocation, whose TS standing has no live native capture for these bytes and the current model: registered without an IPC capture, or read against a current model that differs from the captured one while keeping the same load-case ids. After U7, Rust and Python, given the invocation argument and requested refs equal to the receipt's case order, read numerically_eligible; TS binds standing to the live native capture (hasNativeMechanicsInvocation: an unchanged, not invalidated capture, unchanged bytes, and the current model equal to the captured one) and reads needs_recompute with RETAINED_PRECISION_NATIVE_CAPTURE_REQUIRED. Stricter; fails closed. Every TS consumer of eligible standing (session Current, the rule-check gate, the T6 panels) also requires hasNativeMechanicsInvocation.
